Instruction: Generate code that creates an emulation environment using the seed-emulator library. The environment should include three types of autonomous systems (AS): transit, stub, and utility. 

For the transit AS, create two internet exchanges with specific display names, three internal networks, and four routers linked in a linear structure. 

For the stub AS, create three different systems. The first two should have an internal network, a router, and two host nodes. The first host node should have additional software installed and a new account created. The third system should be created using a utility function and further customized.

Establish BGP peering by creating an Ebgp layer and setting up the transit AS as the internet service provider for all the stub ASes. Also, set up direct peering between two of the stub ASes.

Create a web service layer with two web service nodes and bind these virtual nodes to physical nodes. 

Add all the created layers to the emulator and save it to a component file. Render the emulator and change the display names for the nodes hosting the web services.

Finally, compile the emulator using Docker, specifying custom images from DockerHub and local sources. Generate Docker files and copy the base container image to the output folder.

```python
from seed_emulator import (
    Emulator, AutonomousSystem, makeTransitAs, makeStubAs, makeStubAsWithHosts,
    createInternetExchange, createNetwork, createRouter, createHost, addLayer,
    Ebgp, WebService, Layer, bind, setDisplayName, addSoftware, createAccount,
    compile, DockerImage, generate, copyFile
)

# Create Emulator
emu = Emulator()

# --- Transit AS ---
transit_as = makeTransitAs(asn=65000, name="Transit-AS")
# Create two Internet Exchanges
ix1 = createInternetExchange(name="IX-Alpha", display_name="Internet Exchange Alpha")
ix2 = createInternetExchange(name="IX-Beta", display_name="Internet Exchange Beta")
transit_as.addInternetExchange(ix1)
transit_as.addInternetExchange(ix2)

# Create three internal networks
net1 = createNetwork(name="TransitNet1")
net2 = createNetwork(name="TransitNet2")
net3 = createNetwork(name="TransitNet3")
transit_as.addNetwork(net1)
transit_as.addNetwork(net2)
transit_as.addNetwork(net3)

# Create four routers in a linear structure
r1 = createRouter(name="TransitR1")
r2 = createRouter(name="TransitR2")
r3 = createRouter(name="TransitR3")
r4 = createRouter(name="TransitR4")
transit_as.addRouter(r1)
transit_as.addRouter(r2)
transit_as.addRouter(r3)
transit_as.addRouter(r4)
# Link routers linearly
r1.joinNetwork(net1)
r2.joinNetwork(net1)
r2.joinNetwork(net2)
r3.joinNetwork(net2)
r3.joinNetwork(net3)
r4.joinNetwork(net3)

# --- Stub ASes ---
stub_as1 = makeStubAs(asn=65100, name="Stub-AS1")
stub_net1 = createNetwork(name="Stub1Net")
stub_as1.addNetwork(stub_net1)
stub_r1 = createRouter(name="Stub1R")
stub_as1.addRouter(stub_r1)
stub_r1.joinNetwork(stub_net1)
stub_host1 = createHost(name="Stub1Host1")
stub_host2 = createHost(name="Stub1Host2")
stub_as1.addHost(stub_host1)
stub_as1.addHost(stub_host2)
stub_host1.joinNetwork(stub_net1)
stub_host2.joinNetwork(stub_net1)
# Install software and create account on host1
addSoftware(stub_host1, "nginx")
createAccount(stub_host1, username="webadmin", password="seedemu123")

stub_as2 = makeStubAs(asn=65101, name="Stub-AS2")
stub_net2 = createNetwork(name="Stub2Net")
stub_as2.addNetwork(stub_net2)
stub_r2 = createRouter(name="Stub2R")
stub_as2.addRouter(stub_r2)
stub_r2.joinNetwork(stub_net2)
stub_host3 = createHost(name="Stub2Host1")
stub_host4 = createHost(name="Stub2Host2")
stub_as2.addHost(stub_host3)
stub_as2.addHost(stub_host4)
stub_host3.joinNetwork(stub_net2)
stub_host4.joinNetwork(stub_net2)

# Third stub AS using utility function and further customized
stub_as3 = makeStubAsWithHosts(asn=65102, name="Stub-AS3", num_hosts=2)
stub_as3.setAttribute("customized", True)
stub_as3.getHost(0).setAttribute("role", "special")

# --- Utility AS ---
utility_as = AutonomousSystem(asn=65200, name="Utility-AS", type="utility")

# --- BGP Peering ---
ebgp_layer = Ebgp()
# Set transit as ISP for all stub ASes
ebgp_layer.addCustomerProvider(stub_as1, transit_as)
ebgp_layer.addCustomerProvider(stub_as2, transit_as)
ebgp_layer.addCustomerProvider(stub_as3, transit_as)
# Direct peering between stub_as1 and stub_as2
ebgp_layer.addPeer(stub_as1, stub_as2)

# --- Web Service Layer ---
web_layer = Layer(name="WebServiceLayer")
web_service1 = WebService(name="WebService1")
web_service2 = WebService(name="WebService2")
web_layer.addService(web_service1)
web_layer.addService(web_service2)
# Bind web services to physical nodes
bind(web_service1, stub_host1)
bind(web_service2, stub_host3)

# --- Add all layers to emulator ---
addLayer(emu, transit_as)
addLayer(emu, stub_as1)
addLayer(emu, stub_as2)
addLayer(emu, stub_as3)
addLayer(emu, utility_as)
addLayer(emu, ebgp_layer)
addLayer(emu, web_layer)

# --- Save to component file ---
emu.save("my_emulation.component")

# --- Render the emulator ---
emu.render()

# --- Change display names for nodes hosting web services ---
setDisplayName(stub_host1, "Web Frontend Alpha")
setDisplayName(stub_host3, "Web Frontend Beta")

# --- Compile the emulator using Docker ---
docker = DockerImage()
docker.addImage("nginx", "dockerhub/nginx:latest")
docker.addImage("customapp", "./local/customapp")
emu.compile(docker)
emu.generateDockerFiles(output_dir="./output")
copyFile("base_container_image.tar", "./output/base_container_image.tar")
```
